docs.summary: Builds a SPIR-V module: allocates result ids, de-duplicates types and constants, and serializes the sections in the order the spec requires (capabilities, memory model, entry points, execution modes, debug, decorations, types/constants/globals, then function bodies). Mirrors the role of glslang's SpvBuilder.

members.name: PostProcessNarrowTypes
members.signature: public void PostProcessNarrowTypes(uint version)

docs.summary: glslang's Builder::postProcessFeatures for the narrow (8/16-bit) arithmetic capabilities. glslang does not add Int8/Int16/Float16 when it declares an 8/16-bit type: a module that only moves narrow values in and out of storage needs just the storage capabilities (and only the device features they imply). The arithmetic capability is added when a constant of the type exists or an instruction in a function body uses it beyond loading, storing, copying or converting it (postProcessType). Pointer types into PhysicalStorageBuffer get their storage capability here too, since such memory has no variable.

members.name: PostProcessImageSignExtension
members.signature: public void PostProcessImageSignExtension()

docs.summary: SPIR-V 1.4's SignExtend/ZeroExtend image operands: from 1.4 on glslang marks every texel-producing or texel-consuming image instruction on a 32-bit integer image with the image's signedness (TGlslangToSpvTraverser's signExtensionMask). Depth-compare forms only ever return float and are left alone.
